trust_decision.summary: Decided: whether a gated principal may change a document's docstatus without a consent marker of its own. At the document layer `_require_consent` (act.py:367) lets an act RIDE an enclosing governed act instead of calling `consent_verdict` (scope.py:1081), which is where a marker is bound to one document and one act; the pinned cancel branch of `_may_ride` says every cancel may ride, so the marker-to-act binding never runs for a nested cancel.

landing_point.why: The advisory says a submit marker licensed cancellation of a caller-named pre-existing document. The only place a cancel can proceed with no marker is `_may_ride`'s CANCEL branch, which at the pinned commit returns True for every cancel (`if action == CANCEL: return True`). An engineer reading the summary starts here.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The advisory names a submit marker licensing a cancel, so a cancel cascading into further cancels reads as ordinary UNDO — ERPNext's own invoice cancel cancels the system-generated credit/debit notes and journals it made, and no human can mint a marker for a name that does not exist until the cancel is running.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A governed CANCEL legitimately cascades into lifecycle cancels of documents the framework generated: an ordinary invoice cancel makes ERPNext cancel the system-generated credit and debit notes, the exchange gain/loss journal and the common-party journal. On the submit side, a document the act created in two calls (`doc.save()` then `doc.submit()`) must also ride. An over-broad fix that demands `flags.in_insert` or a fresh marker on every nested cancel refuses UNDO and aborts the enclosing act, and requiring a second marker without letting one request carry two makes an asset-sale submit impossible.
O5_coupled_behaviour.where: guard/pacioli_guard/act.py:273-280 (pinned residual statement); pinned by the fix's own tests at fix.diff:1306-1319 and fix.diff:1321-1338

O8_uncovered_routes.route: A write that reaches the document lifecycle with `flags.ignore_validate` set makes `run_before_save_methods` return early, so `before_submit`/`before_cancel` never fire and the consent gate never runs (ERPNext pos_invoice_merge_log.py:431-432 and stock_controller.py:2517-2521 per act.py); the fix does not touch this route.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The flag is not remotely settable (frappe's RESERVED_KEYWORDS reject it and frappe.call's get_newargs pops it), so it is documented as a coverage limit rather than an attacker lever.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Writes that skip the document lifecycle entirely move docstatus with no consent gate: raw SQL, `db_update`/`db_set` field writes, and `Document.discard` (whitelisted; sets docstatus = 2 via db_set and fires before_discard instead of before_cancel). The fix does not touch this route.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: No Frappe extension point observes these writes; the README already publishes them as residuals, and discard refuses anything that is not a draft so no ledger entry is ever reversed.
